issues.display_title: Issue #122: Integrate Countly analytics with per-domain app keys
issues.main_description_html:
Goal

Integrate Countly product analytics into the maps frontend using the official countly-sdk-web package.

Scope

  • Add countly-sdk-web dependency.
  • Root-level client component that initializes the SDK in the browser only.
  • Automatic session tracking, page view tracking on App Router route change, and JS error tracking.
  • Per-domain configuration: the app is served from several hosts, and each production host reports to its own Countly app key.
    • maps.gothru.co -> GoThru app key
    • maps.panorra.com -> Panorra app key
    • Any other host (localhost, *.local, dev/preview domains) reports nothing.

Notes

  • Countly app_key is a write-only ingestion key that ships in the browser bundle, so it lives in src/config/config.ts next to the existing domainSourceConfig rather than in env vars. A single build serves multiple domains, so env vars cannot select per host.
  • The Countly dashboard api_key is a real secret and must never be committed.

Pending

  • Fill in the two production app keys and the Countly server URL.

RESULT

Countly is live on development.

  • Added countly-sdk-web@26.1.3 (ships its own type declarations; the module is SSR-safe, it guards browser globals behind an isBrowser check).
  • New src/app/countly.tsx, a root-level client component mounted in src/app/layout.tsx. It initializes the SDK inside useEffect, so it never runs during SSR, and then calls track_sessions(), track_errors() and track_pageview(path) on every App Router route change via usePathname.
  • New countlyConfig in src/config/config.ts, keyed by window.location.host in the same shape as the existing domainSourceConfig:
    • maps.gothru.co and maps.panorra.com each report to their own app key, both against https://data.gothru.co.
    • Any host absent from the map never initializes the SDK, so localhost, *.local and preview domains send nothing.

Env vars were deliberately not used: one build serves several domains, so NEXT_PUBLIC_* cannot select per host. The app_key is a write-only ingestion key that already ships inside the browser bundle, so keeping it in config leaks nothing; the Countly dashboard api_key remains out of this repo.

Verification: npx tsc --noEmit clean, npx eslint clean on the touched files, and the running dev server returns 200 with the Countly chunk present in the rendered HTML.

Not included, add later if wanted: track_clicks / track_scrolls / track_links / track_forms, consent management, request checksum via the SDK salt option, and excluding /embed routes from tracking.

Commit: 0ae4f15 (merged as d653080)
Branch: feature/122-integrate-countly-analytics-with-per -> development

issues.display_title: Issue #123: feat: add trackEvent helper for Countly events
issues.main_description_html:
Goal

One place to fire Countly custom events, so no component has to import the SDK directly.

Scope

  • New helper (src/helpers/countly.ts) exporting trackEvent(key, segmentation?).
  • It must no-op safely when the SDK never initialized — on localhost, *.local and any host absent from countlyConfig, Countly.init() is never called, and the helper is imported by components that run there too.
  • Segmentation values must be flat primitives; Countly drops nested objects.
  • src/app/countly.tsx stays the only place that calls Countly.init().

Why first

The other seven tracking tasks all depend on this helper. Merge this to development before starting them, so their branches do not each re-invent it.

Acceptance

  • npx tsc --noEmit clean, npx eslint clean.
  • Calling trackEvent() on a host with no Countly config does not throw and does not warn.

issues.display_title: Issue #124: track: map lifecycle and zoom
issues.main_description_html:
Events

Event Location Segmentation
map_loaded src/hooks/useMapLoad.ts:13 (handleMapLoad) initial zoom (event.target.getZoom()), embed flag (window.self !== window.top)
map_zoom_changed src/components/main/maps/container/main/MapEvent.tsx:133 (handleZoomEnd) zoom bucket, whether markers/lines are above their visibility threshold

Why

map_loaded is the denominator for every ratio in the other tracking tasks — without it, a click count means nothing. Zoom is the strongest intent signal on this map, because markers and lines only render above markersVisibleZoomLevels / linesVisibleZoomLevels; the zoom distribution explains why users see an empty map.

Notes

handleZoomEnd fires on every zoom gesture. Send the zoom rounded to an integer bucket rather than the raw float, so the segmentation does not explode into hundreds of distinct values.

Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

Events

Event Location Segmentation
moderation_point_clicked src/components/main/maps/source/moderations/ModerationMapEvents.tsx:46 (handleLayerClick -> openTour) feature.layer.id (one of the four marker layers), pano_id, tour_key, embed flag
moderation_line_clicked same file :140 (handleLinesClick) layer id, tour_key, resolved nearest pano id, candidate count, whether the resolution found nothing

Why

These are the two ways a user enters a tour. Splitting by feature.layer.id shows which of the four marker layers (id circles, hosted tours, SV publishing, google publish) actually drives tour opens.

The line click carries the more interesting signal: when nearest.id resolves to null the click is a dead click — the user tapped the road line and nothing happened. That failure is currently invisible.

Notes

Cursor lngLat is a map coordinate, not the user's position, so it is safe to send. Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

Events

Event Location Segmentation
panorra_marker_clicked src/components/main/maps/source/panorra/PanorraMapEvents.tsx:179 (handleClick on panorraThumbnailLayer) slug, category (1 Leisure / 2 Real Estate / 3 Business), zoom, embed flag, mobile flag
panorra_view_panorama_clicked src/components/main/maps/ui/CustomPopup.tsx:120 (handleViewPanorama) slug, category, embedded-context flag

Why

Together these give the popup-to-detail click-through rate, and separate the embedded postMessage exit from the standalone new-tab exit. Desktop and mobile take different paths at the marker click (desktop opens panorra.com directly, mobile shows the popup first), so the mobile flag is what makes the funnel readable.

Privacy rules (apply to every event here)

Never attach username, fullname, avatar, userId, businessName, address, or raw search text to an event. Use content identifiers only: slug, cid, category, type, city, country. These fields are in scope at several of the call sites below, so exclusion has to be deliberate.

feature.properties at the marker call site is a PanorraStateType carrying the post author's username, fullname and address. Send slug and category only.

Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

Event

Event Location Segmentation
photographer_marker_clicked src/components/main/maps/source/photographer/hooks/usePhotographerMapEvents.ts:68 (handleClick on photographerLayer) slug, type (main | api), city, country, isSublocation, rating band

Why

Marketplace discovery signal: which photographers get opened, and whether main-location pins outperform sublocation/api pins.

Notes

Every click triggers a getPhotographerDetail fetch — worth attaching the response outcome so a slow or failing lookup shows up here rather than staying silent.

Privacy rules (apply to every event here)

Never attach username, fullname, avatar, userId, businessName, address, or raw search text to an event. Use content identifiers only: slug, cid, category, type, city, country. These fields are in scope at several of the call sites below, so exclusion has to be deliberate.

props.fullname, props.avatar and props.userId identify a real person and are in scope at this call site. Exclude all three.

Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

Events

Event Location Segmentation
search_performed src/components/search/InputSearch.tsx:82 result_count, query_length, not the query text
search_zero_results same file :108 query_length

Why

Nobody currently knows whether the search box is used at all. Zero-result queries are the actionable half: they say the data is missing, not the feature.

Privacy — the deciding constraint

Raw query text must not be sent. Users type home addresses into a map search box, which would put personal data into analytics. Send result_count and query_length only.

Do not track per-keystroke input (InputSearch.tsx:119) — it is both a flood and the worst version of the privacy problem.

Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

Event

tour_dwell_time — a timed event using the SDK's start_event(key) / end_event(key, segmentation) pair rather than add_event.

Where

Start when a tour opens (src/components/main/maps/source/moderations/ModerationMapEvents.tsx:39, openTour). End when the tour closes, the route changes, or the page unloads.

Why

Click counts say a tour was opened; only duration says whether it was worth opening. This is the single most valuable signal for a maps product and the only one that needs the timed-event API.

Notes

The end call has to be reachable from every exit path — route change via usePathname, and visibilitychange / pagehide for tab close. A start without an end sends nothing at all, so the exit paths are the whole task.

Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

issues.display_title: Issue #130: track: report silent failures Countly cannot see
issues.main_description_html:
Why this is separate

Countly.track_errors() only captures uncaught JS errors. Every failure below is swallowed by a catch block, so it will never appear in Countly no matter how often it breaks a user's session.

Events

Event Location What breaks for the user
tile_request_failed src/app/data/[source]/[z]/[x]/[y]/route.ts:101 map renders with holes, silently
tile_cache_degraded same file :121 Redis down, falls back, user just sees it get slow
map_style_blank_render src/hooks/useResolvedMapStyle.ts:92 base style transform fails -> blank map
thumbnail_placeholder_served src/app/thumbnail-v2/[slug]/route.ts:76 thumbnail silently becomes a placeholder
pano_position_lookup_failed src/components/main/maps/container/main/PostMessage.tsx:19 position lookup fails inside an embed

Notes

The first four are server-side or near it; check whether each call site runs in the browser before firing a web SDK event, and skip or route differently the ones that do not.

Segmentation should carry the failure reason and the identifier involved (source name, slug, tile z/x/y) — never a full stack trace or a URL with credentials in it.

Depends on the trackEvent helper task.

RESULT

Three of the five call sites are done. Two are not, and cannot be with this SDK.

Done (client-side)

Event Location
map_error src/components/main/maps/container/main/MapContainer.tsx onError
map_style_transform_failed src/hooks/useResolvedMapStyle.ts
pano_position_lookup_failed src/components/main/maps/container/main/PostMessage.tsx

Verified against a local Countly sink: forcing tile fetches to fail produced real map_error payloads. That surfaced two pre-existing defects that had only ever been console.warn'd:

  • The layer 'panorraLeisureSourceLayerCirlces' does not exist in the map's style and cannot be queried
  • Source layer "railway" does not exist on source "openmaptiles" as specified by style layer "bridge-r...

Both are worth their own issue.

Not done, and why

tile_request_failed, tile_cache_degraded and thumbnail_placeholder_served live in route handlers (src/app/data/[source]/[z]/[x]/[y]/route.ts is marked 'use server', and src/app/thumbnail-v2/[slug]/route.ts is a route handler). countly-sdk-web is a browser SDK — it has no way to run there, so these were left out rather than faked.

Reporting them needs a server-side SDK (countly-sdk-nodejs) as a separate task. map_error partly compensates in the meantime: a tile the route failed to serve still surfaces as a client-side map error, though without the server's reason for the failure.

Note

All reason strings are truncated to 100 characters so no URL or stack trace reaches the analytics payload.
